key: We should blunt our sharp points, and unravel the complications of things; we should attemper our brightness, and bring ourselves into agreement with the obscurity of others.
s: Between images of the Tao’s emptiness and stillness, the chapter turns to conduct; the Heshang Gong commentary, on chapter 4, takes it as checking the keen pursuit of merit and fame, untying knotted resentment, and sharing the common dust rather than standing apart.
src: The Heshang Gong commentary, Laozi Daodejing Heshang Gong zhangju, chapter 4, zh.wikisource, revision 2019760 (2021)

evidence.words: 人欲銳精進取功名，當挫止之 … 紛，結恨也。當念道無為以解釋。 … 當與眾庶同垢塵，不當自別殊。
evidence.gloss: (On blunting sharp points:) when a person wants to press keenly forward to seize merit and fame, he should check it and stop. … (On unravelling complications:) complications are knotted resentments; one should think on the non-action of the Tao to untie them. … (On agreeing with the dust:) one should share the grime and dust of the common people and not set oneself apart.

reason: The problem holds: the old sentence ran 63 words and its plain sense restated the key verse clause by clause. Rewritten to rules 1 and 2: the plain sense now gives only context (the verse stands between the chapter’s images of the Tao as empty and as still, and turns to conduct), repeats no four-word run of the key verse and leans on none of Legge’s parentheses. The reading keeps the Heshang Gong commentary and its three glosses from the same packet text (挫其銳, 解其紛, 同其塵), shortened: the clause on following the self-concealing Tao, which the refuter flagged as a soft rendering of 法道不自見, is dropped, so nothing now goes beyond the words. Key, ref, at and src unchanged. verse.js ok (Tao Te Ching 4, at [3]); entry-check ok, no warns; 43 words.
